title: Verify Fargate cannot host a WireGuard peer
description:
## Question

**Can ECS Fargate host a WireGuard peer?**

`chatticus-fbae4e` D2 asserts it cannot — Fargate supports neither privileged mode nor `NET_ADMIN` / `/dev/net/tun` — and marks the claim *"verify before implementation."*

This is a **documentation check, not a spike.** Recorded as a task so nobody spends a day building a Fargate-based tunnel endpoint on an unverified assumption, and so nobody spends a day *proving* something a doc page settles in minutes.

## Why it matters

If the assertion is wrong and Fargate *can* run a WireGuard peer, the tunnel endpoint becomes scale-to-zero rather than a stopped-when-idle EC2 instance. That drops the idle floor from ~$0.65/mo to $0 and removes a box to patch — a genuine improvement to D2, not a rounding error, given the initiative's cost argument turns on idle floors.

If the assertion is right, D2 stands as written and the "verify" caveat comes out.

## How

Check the ECS task definition documentation for `linuxParameters.capabilities.add` support on the Fargate launch type, and for privileged mode. If ambiguous, attempt a task definition requesting `NET_ADMIN` and observe whether registration or task start is rejected.

## Cost

Minutes.

## Done when

`chatticus-fbae4e` D2 either drops its "verify before implementation" caveat, or is corrected along with the endpoint cost figures that depend on it.

comments.text:
## Result: Fargate cannot host a WireGuard peer

D2 confirmed. The verify caveat on `chatticus-fbae4e` D2 is removed.

### Phase 1 — AWS documentation

| Claim | Source | Finding |
|-------|--------|---------|
| No privileged containers | [Fargate task definition differences](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html) | `privileged` is **not valid** on Fargate |
| No privileged containers | [Fargate security considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-security-considerations.html) | Privileged containers **unavailable** on Fargate |
| `NET_ADMIN` restricted | [Fargate security considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-security-considerations.html) | `CAP_NET_ADMIN` and `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` **restricted** |
| Only `SYS_PTRACE` addable | [Fargate task definition differences](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html) | `linuxParameters.capabilities.add` allows **only** `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` |
| Only `SYS_PTRACE` addable | [API KernelCapabilities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_KernelCapabilities.html) | *"Tasks launched on AWS Fargate only support adding the `SYS_PTRACE` kernel capability."* |
| No `/dev/net/tun` device mapping | [Fargate task definition differences](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/fargate-tasks-services.html) | `linuxParameters.devices` **not supported** on Fargate |

WireGuard requires `NET_ADMIN` (interface creation) and a TUN device; Fargate provides neither.

### Phase 2 — live API probe

- **Account:** 335163751677 (root)
- **Region:** us-east-1
- **Cluster:** `ChatticusComputers-ClusterEB0386A7-KBVRNWeg2bzf` (existence confirmed; not used for RunTask)
- **Task definition:** `spike-wg-cap-check-0b10d6` with `requiresCompatibilities: ["FARGATE"]`, `linuxParameters.capabilities.add: ["NET_ADMIN"]`
- **Command:** `aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://spike-task-def-net-admin.json`

**Outcome:** Registration rejected at API — no task definition created, nothing to deregister.

```
ClientException: NET_ADMIN is not allowed on Fargate.
```

RunTask was not attempted (registration failed).

### Conclusion

- D2 stands: tunnel endpoint remains **stopped-when-idle EC2** (~$0.65/mo EBS-only idle floor).
- Fargate scale-to-zero tunnel endpoint is **not** available on current ECS Fargate.
- Spike artifacts live in worktree `/tmp/chatticus-0b10d6-fargate-wg` on branch `spike/fargate-wireguard-0b10d6`.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Learnings

- **Do not design a Fargate WireGuard endpoint.** Current ECS Fargate rejects `NET_ADMIN` at `RegisterTaskDefinition` (`ClientException: NET_ADMIN is not allowed on Fargate`). Privileged mode and `linuxParameters.devices` (`/dev/net/tun`) are also unsupported.
- Generic task-definition enums listing `NET_ADMIN` are not Fargate permission. An ECS-on-EC2 WireGuard task would have been a false positive.
- Userspace UDP proxies are not a WireGuard peer. The D2 economics (stopped EC2, ~$0.65/mo EBS idle) do not change.
- Verification needed both the Fargate-specific docs and a live API probe; the probe is what we will quote later.
